checks.reason: The opening captures the possibility that the identification categories are career stages and proposes testing the unreported transitions against tenure.
It preserves the contrast between concessions made during outsider encounters and favorable reinterpretations afterward, and proposes observing both moments.
It changes departure before prolonged socialization into departure before socialization at all and assumes that high sales rank establishes prior identification and fully completed practices.
It treats the absence of reported earlier dreams or later mentoring failures as proof those events never occurred and calls a car belonging to someone else a stranger’s car.
It attributes identification to freely chosen costly enactments rather than preexisting discontent and proposes testing the sequence of action and stated dissatisfaction.
It captures the reading’s reversal of causation, in which not recruiting preserves outside ties, and proposes checking whether recruitment or criticism came first.
It presents the link between accounting choices and organizational allegiance as established even though the reading explicitly offers it as an untested possibility.
It shifts the test from whether support depends on performing Amway work to whether the personal relationship predates Amway, a distinction the reading does not make.
It correctly emphasizes mentoring and role modeling within the shopping trip over acquiring desired goods and proposes comparing early outings to test that emphasis.
It characterizes seekership as dissatisfaction brought into Amway and reinterpreted there, and proposes following that dissatisfaction across entry and later life changes.
It preserves the claim that dream building creates and renews identity shortfalls before mentoring begins and proposes testing the order of those encounters.
It treats reactions by existing contacts as a possible source of the social conditions shaping identification and proposes tracing those reactions and their effects.
It distinguishes unmeasured net financial position from observed sales volume and proposes comparing financial flows across identification groups.
It separates excitement about imagined futures from dissatisfaction with present life and proposes testing which is associated with subsequent identification.
It locates the proposed difference between detached and oppositional leavers in unresolved grievance despite weak mentor ties in both and suggests reconstructing each sequence.
It captures the proposal that dream building operates through the mentor relationship and would test whether dreams change independently of that bond.
It preserves the account of identification states as different ways of reckoning participation costs and proposes tracking financial judgments alongside continued membership or exit.
